state.objective: Choose a production dependency for a compiler migration whose endpoint is no third-party SQLite parser source checked into Can. Only standard pinned Go modules using the common module cache meet the requested boundary; copied code in any language and repository-stored archives/checkouts do not. Keep raw-SQL checking and execution through Bun.SQL. There are zero external users and no compatibility obligation. The established workflow uses Muse implementation and independent Codex verification, with neither large builds nor measurements allowed on the 256GB laptop.
state.contract: Both candidates must feed the existing compiler Analysis boundary with exact UTF-8 byte extents, complete source-ordered bind locations/numbers, statement type/count, outermost LIMIT shape, RETURNING flags and diagnostic positions. Higher layers retain single-statement rules, declared-name/coverage checks, the unique trailing limit slot, ordinary mutation execute, and one-row INSERT RETURNING admission. Native templates and runtime row decoding consume that analysis. No schema correctness or universal query-work bound is established. Metadata should identify parser content/release rather than confuse Tree-sitter language ABI with identity. Keep PostgreSQL CGo and pre-provisioned offline distribution settings CGO_ENABLED=1/GOPROXY=off.
state.official: The official-binding option has been built and exercised: github.com/defin/tree-sitter-sqlite3 v0.1.1-0.20260503135658-7f69bb66845b plus github.com/tree-sitter/go-tree-sitter v0.25.0 admits ABI15 and reproduces the old analysis for 74 inputs. Its parser, scanner and header are byte-identical to the current pinned grammar, and module archives contain the compile inputs. Runtime commit adc13ffd8b2c0b01b878fda9f7c422ce0df5fad3 resolves through proxy and sums even though GitHub no longer exposes that release tag. Integration must close each parser/tree/cursor once, detect missing nodes and special malformed-literal nodes, and cap an iterative walk. The simple Parse entry avoids a suspected options callback pointer-retention issue. External packages continue to compile C via CGo.
state.meyer: The second candidate, github.com/sqlc-dev/meyer v0.1.2, was resolved and sum-verified at 59b2dbf9b1872316bc6c6d3379b500df84db3e01. This independent MIT parser uses only Go, requires Go1.24 and lists no module dependencies. sqlc has integrated it on main but not in the release inspected here; it remains a recent dependency. A 74-input qualification supplies all needed syntax structures and byte ranges through Unicode text, CTE/subquery limits, mutations and RETURNING expressions. Divergences cover named-sigil identity, digit/Tcl parameters, optional UPDATE/DELETE LIMIT, failure presentation and inclusion of trailing semicolons in spans. Its comma LIMIT visits count before offset, requiring sorting by source position. BindParam.Number gives native numbering directly, avoiding Can-owned reimplementation.
state.guards_and_limits: Guard the adapter rather than claim either library is resource-isolated. Meyer's built-in depth ceiling is 10000; correctness probes accepted 40035-byte expression chains, parentheses nested5000 and a chain of100000 terms, rejecting nesting15000 normally. There are no performance or allocation measurements. ParseString permits a pre-parse 1MiB byte cap, unlike the context-ignoring unbounded reader API. Refuse embedded NUL because its lexer stops there. An iterative Children traversal with a million-node budget avoids recursive ast.Walk depth growth; ordered, checked byte spans follow. This is not a hard memory/time guarantee. Comparable small Tree-sitter probes passed, though C allocation exhaustion aborts. No full upstream corpus, multi-platform qualification or staged bundle test has been executed.
state.verified_policy: Bun1.4.2 SQLite was exercised independently in memory: :a/@a/$a carried three different supplied values; $1 worked as a name; X'01001' and 123abc failed. Preparation of #name succeeded, yet that sigil is outside Can's stated source family. The prior engine-equivalence explanation for name-sigil collapse and digit-name failure is false, and no separate compatibility reason justifies retaining it. Named sites must still match declared Can field suffixes (numeric or Tcl application names may fail that check), while limit names have no declaration. Avoid copying old semicolon exclusion into an otherwise precise upstream span API. Intended rules and executed SQLite results resolve disagreements, not the existence of older expected outputs.
state.engine_arbitration: Final oracle evidence from Bun1.4.2 with SQLite3.54.0 and real in-memory tables verifies named numeric/Tcl parameters and distinct sigils, as well as executable UPDATE/DELETE LIMIT. Set Meyer's Options{UpdateDeleteLimit:true} accordingly. Can's existing CheckSites closes the shared parser acceptance of zero/overflow parameter numbers; preserving that validation avoids duplicate binding logic. A LIMIT on an earlier compound core is accepted by both parsers but rejected by SQLite, so apply a small structural nonfinal-core LIMIT/ORDER BY rejection rather than reproduce native preparation. The engine's nesting2000 pass/5000 failure differs from both parsers; compiler byte/node budgets should stand independently without a bespoke depth lexer or a promise that every parsed statement prepares. There is no evidenced reason to create a Can-owned external parser repository.

production_parser.instructions: Recommend the parser choice to ship for the authorized migration based only on these supplied qualifications, guard requirements and maintenance uncertainties. Retain intended SQL validation, exclude presumed performance gains, and treat the selection as advice subject to independent code verification.

criteria.meyer: Choose v0.1.2 of Meyer, consuming its numbered AST with length/NUL validation and a limited nonrecursive sorted occurrence walk. Revise metadata and justified admission expectations while eliminating copied SQLite C and custom serialization.
criteria.official: Prefer the tested Tree-sitter Go binding/runtime pins, using a small lifecycle-aware bounded adapter and explicit syntax/parameter corrections. Delete the local upstream payload; its C implementation continues through the shared module cache.
criteria.further_evidence: Withhold selection pending another small verification that materially affects suitability; stay within existing external modules and the present SQL contract rather than expanding architecture.
